# The provenance file on Clementia

*Catalogue entry — Clementia. Every claim below carries its chain of custody.*

## Provenance

**1. The attestation.** **CLEMENTIA**, from the tradition's own record. On record: Seneca, De Clementia, Cicero, Pro Marcello and Pro Ligario, Oxford Latin Dictionary, s.v. clementia, Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary, s.v. clementia.

**2. The narrative record.** **The Clemency of Caesar** — Julius Caesar made clementia the signature of his dictatorship.  Through the civil war of 49–45 BCE he pardoned one defeated enemy after another — Cicero, Ligarius, the consular Marcellus, and at last Brutus and Cassius themselves, whom he admitted to office. **Clementia Augusti** — The emperors inherited the gesture and made it a system.  Under Nero the mint of Rome struck sestertii and dupondii showing Clementia as a standing woman, patera in hand, pouring a libation over an altar — legend CLEMENTIA AVGVSTI — and the type recurs across the coinage of the first two centuries.

**3. The physical record.** Clementia's monuments are numismatic above all. Nero's sestertii and dupondii of 64–66 CE show her standing with patera and cornucopia before a lighted altar, legend CLEMENTIA AVGVSTI S C, among the most beautiful personifications on Roman coinage; later emperors revived the type whenever they needed the message. In stone, a Temple of Clementia Caesaris stood at Rome, voted by the senate in 45 BCE in Caesar's honor, with the dictator's own statue installed as the goddess's image — a shrine that was also, his enemies noted, a claim to divinity on the republic's own ground. No certain remains of the temple have been identified. Personified virtues in general crowded imperial art — on the Ara Pacis, in the Forum of Nerva, on gems and cameos — but Clementia's own dossier is bronze and silver: the empire's most widely circulated theology.

**4. The current holding.** The temple at [/clementia/](/clementia/), classified Tier 2. Tier-2 here means one preserved truth — not less important, just singular. The temple shows it and names it.

**5. The documented resonances.** **Education, Research & Knowledge**, **Mythic Name Restoration**, **Writing, Publishing & Media** — seats argued and weighted in the [pattern atlas](/patterns/), read through the myths in this temple's [Resonance File](/clementia/blog/resonance/).

**6. The primary sources.** [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the library this file answers to, open at the [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/).

**7. The continuing record.** Clementia remains a living concept in law and politics.  Executive clemency, the power to pardon or commute sentences, is one of the oldest prerogatives of rulers.
